cohort: The study included 400 pregnant women, divided into groups with and without Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), from the Gynecology and Obstetrics Clinic of Ayatollah Mousavi Hospital in Zanjan, Iran, from 2019 to 2020.
finding: Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) have a significantly increased likelihood of spontaneous abortion, preterm labor, cesarean section, and delivering a low-birth-weight infant.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most prevalent adverse outcome, with women with SLE having an 18.9 times higher likelihood of undergoing a cesarean section compared to those without SLE.
